title: Starter Integration Live-Ref Quicknotes
content:
Purpose:
A compact, practical runbook to get an engineer from 0 to a reproducible SDK integration that uses live reference data (live-ref) for prompt context. This is intentionally short, action-focused, and meant for pairing sessions or a 30–60 minute workshop.

Persona:
- Backend engineer or ML engineer who needs a low-friction SDK flow to wire Redwood API calls into an existing service.
- Goals: first successful request, baseline telemetry, safety and fallback for production.

Time-to-first-success (target): 15 minutes
Prerequisites:
- Redwood API key in env: REDWOOD_API_KEY
- Local node/python runtime (examples below)
- Repo checkout: git clone git@github.com:redwood-inference/example-live-ref-app.git
- Small sample dataset (CSV/JSON) with ephemeral identifiers; do not use PII in workshop

Quickstart (15-min path):
1) Checkout lightweight starter: cd example-live-ref-app && ./scripts/bootstrap.sh
2) Set API key: export REDWOOD_API_KEY=sk.test_xxx
3) Start dev server that hosts live-ref endpoint: ./scripts/run-local-live-ref.sh (serves /live-ref/sample.json)
4) Install SDK (dev wheel): pip install -e ../sdk/python || npm i ../sdk/js --no-audit
5) Minimal call (python):
   from redwood import RedwoodClient
   client = RedwoodClient(api_key=os.environ['REDWOOD_API_KEY'])
   ctx = open('fixtures/live-ref-sample.json').read()
   resp = client.chat.create(messages=[{"role":"system","content":"You are a helpful assistant."}, {"role":"user","content":"Summarize the user notes: " + ctx}], model="rwd-compact-1")
   print(resp.text)
6) Verify response, capture request-id from headers for telemetry.

Smoke tests (what to check immediately):
- 200 OK and model text returned
- Token usage present in response metadata
- Request-id mapped to local trace id
- Live-ref payload size <= 64KB (enforce early)

Integration checklist (short):
- [ ] Default timeout set to 6s for interactive flows
- [ ] Retries: idempotent requests have 2 retries with exponential backoff
- [ ] Circuit breaker: open after 5 consecutive 5xxs for 30s
- [ ] Live-ref size validation and truncate strategy documented
- [ ] Prefix caching: enable KV cache for static preamble text
- [ ] Telemetry: emit metrics below on every request

Suggested telemetry keys (minimal):
- redwood.request.count
- redwood.request.latency_ms
- redwood.tokens.requested
- redwood.tokens.response
- redwood.live_ref.size_bytes
- redwood.model.fallback_count
- redwood.request.errors (tagged by code)

Rollout plan (canary):
- Day 0: internal alpha, 5 users (team only), sample traffic recorded
- Canary: 1% of traffic -> compare latency and token spend to baseline for 48h
- Auto-fallback: if 99th percentile latency > baseline + 1200ms OR token spend > baseline * 1.25, route to smaller model variant and alert channel #dev-live-ref

Failure modes and mitigations:
- Live-ref too large -> truncate oldest context and set a flag to surface missing pieces to user.
- Model hallucination on structured fields -> add schema enforcement and a second-pass verifier (lightweight rule-based) before accepting output.
- Rate-limited by provider -> graceful degrade: show cached answer or “partial results” UX and schedule background refresh.

Developer UX copy (in-app):
- Loading: "Finding the freshest notes — this may take a few seconds"
- Fallback message: "We couldn't fetch the latest context right now — showing a recent snapshot"

Docs pointer (what to expand for final PRD):
- Detailed SDK examples for Node/Python/Go (including async streaming examples)
- Live-ref privacy checklist and sample sanitizers for common PII formats
- Exact telemetry sampling rates and retention guidance
- Benchmarks for different live-ref size buckets (0-1KB, 1-16KB, 16-64KB)

Open questions / Decisions to make:
- Default live-ref size limit: 64KB vs 128KB? (trade-off: latency vs signal)
- Who owns the production alert: eng-sre or eng-devexp? Recommend eng-sre own critical on-call; devexp owns runbook and docs.
- Should live-ref requests be billed differently (extra token pre- and post-processing)? Finance input needed.

Next steps (owners):
- Marco: prototype truncation library (due 2025-01-17)
- Sofia: write privacy sanitizers (due 2025-01-24)
- Jonas: add canary routing patch to gateway (PR planned by 2025-01-20)
- Aisha: consolidate final quickstart into repo README and craft 30-min workshop script (due 2025-02-05)

Notes to self (pairing hints):
- Keep the first demo extremely repeatable: same fixture file, deterministic model param set, and explicit env var snapshots.
- Avoid too many feature toggles in first demo; demonstrate one fallback path only.
- Record a 5-minute Loom showing the 15-min path for new hires.

Versioning: v0.2 (working).

TODO (short):
- [ ] Add JS streaming example
- [ ] Add Go minimal client snippet
- [ ] Add step-by-step hotspot for observability (how to trace request-id end-to-end)

End of quicknotes.
